supporting_observations.claim: Several proxy-bound connections recur at roughly five-minute intervals and have closely similar byte counts: about 9.5–9.8 KB sent and 43.5 KB received. This pattern is consistent with the inventory description of PixelForge’s updater checking approximately every five minutes, but does not identify the application or destination.
The cited recurring flows are recorded as connections from WS-LMARTINS-01 to the internal proxy at 10.40.20.30:8080; these records do not show the external HTTPS destination.
At 14:06:11, a proxy-bound connection had substantially smaller byte counts than the recurring flows, so it does not match their observed byte-count pattern.

Later proxy records show Chrome requests by leo.martins to Google Calendar and SharePoint, with associated browser requests to Google-hosted calendar resources and Microsoft/OneDrive-related resources; these records do not establish the destination or process for the recurring flows.

known_telemetry_limitations: For the recurring connections, the supplied records show Zeek connection metadata to the internal proxy but no corresponding proxy request details naming the HTTPS host or URL.
The supplied records do not associate the recurring connections with a process or executable.
The available records cover selected events; absence of a recorded malicious event here does not establish that none occurred.
claims_not_established: That PixelForge’s updater generated the recurring connections.
The external destinations, requested resources, or content of the recurring HTTPS traffic.
Whether the recurring traffic was authorized or malicious based on destination reputation or endpoint inspection.
